title: Exact Lindbladian Dynamics from Conformal Embeddings and Topological Defects in Conformal Field Theory
abstract: Analyzing the dynamics of physical observables in open quantum many-body systems is a fundamental but highly challenging task that has yielded very few exact results. In this work, we identify intrinsic conformal structures that restore exact solvability in $(1+1)$D conformal field theories. For $N$ Majorana fermions with linear mode jumps, the adjoint Lindbladian is triangular on reduced even Majorana monomials, yielding recursive exact Heisenberg evolution. In Wess-Zumino-Witten models admitting conformal Majorana embeddings, this hierarchy gives exact dynamics of affine-current products realized as Majorana bilinears, including regimes where the Kac-Moody current algebra alone does not close. In diagonal rational conformal field theories, Verlinde topological defect lines furnish jump operators whose primary-sector dynamics is exactly diagonal: topological-charge probabilities are conserved, while intersector coherences dephase at rates fixed by the modular $S$ matrix and nonnegative measurement strengths. These examples show that intrinsic conformal structures, such as conformal embeddings and modular data, can organize exactly solvable open conformal dynamics.
summary: This paper develops methods to find exact solutions for the dynamics of open quantum many-body systems within Conformal Field Theory. By exploiting intrinsic conformal structures—like Majorana embeddings and topological defect lines—the authors show that complex dissipative processes can be mathematically organized, leading to conserved quantities or predictable exponential decay of coherence.
main_problem: The core challenge is finding exact solutions for the dynamics of physical observables in open quantum many-body systems governed by Lindblad master equations.
main_result: Intrinsic conformal structures, such as conformal embeddings and modular data, can organize exactly solvable open dynamics in CFTs, leading to conserved topological charges or predictable dephasing rates.
method: The authors employ advanced techniques from Conformal Field Theory (CFT), including analyzing Majorana fermion representations, utilizing Wess-Zumino-Witten models via conformal embeddings, and constructing Lindbladians using Verlinde topological defect lines.
model_or_system: The study focuses on (1+1)D CFTs, specifically N Majorana fermions and WZW models. The dynamics are described by the adjoint Lindbladian acting on operators within these highly constrained quantum field theories.
key_observables: Topological-charge probabilities, intersector coherences ($P_{ab}$), expectation values of current products ($\langle \mathcal{J}^a_n \cdots angle$), and the trace distance $D(ho(t), \Pi(ho(0)))$.
important_parameters: Modular S matrix elements, coupling rates ($\gamma_\pm$), conformal dimensions ($h$), and the dephasing rate $\Gamma_V$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on identifying specific intrinsic conformal structures (embeddings, defect lines) that enforce solvability; limitations are noted when general current algebra closure fails or when considering non-linear products of Virasoro generators.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing exact solvability for Majorana fermions via triangular Lindbladians. It then extends this to WZW models using conformal embeddings, and finally analyzes diagonal RCFTs where dynamics are governed by topological defect lines leading to coherence dephasing.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful theoretical framework for understanding how environmental coupling (dissipation) can be exactly solved in highly structured quantum systems like CFTs, offering insights applicable to open quantum systems beyond standard Markovian approximations.
